verifications.claim: The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1967.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Ratified in 1967" (R2); "added to the U.S. Constitution in 1967" (R3); "ratified on Feb. 10, 1967" (R6); "ratified on February 10, 1967" (R7); "ratified by the states in 1967" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the ratification year as 1967.

verifications.claim: The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified following President John F. Kennedy's assassination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The need for a succession amendment came to light when President John F. Kennedy was assassinated" (R1); "gained traction after President John F. Kennedy's 1963 assassination" (R3); "the assassination of President John F. Kennedy in 1963 which finally pushed Congress" (R7); history post-Kennedy assassination leading to ratification (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the amendment was proposed and ratified after Kennedy's 1963 assassination, directly linking it as a response.

verifications.claim: Section 1 of the 25th Amendment explicitly states that if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Section 1... if the President dies, resigns, or is removed... the Vice President 'shall become President'" (R2); "Section 1. In case of the removal of the President from office or of his death or resignation, the Vice President shall become President" (R5); matching text (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from constitutional text in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Section 2 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to nominate a new Vice President if the office becomes vacant.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Section 2 states that in the event of a vice-presidential vacancy, the president will nominate a vice president" (R1); "Section 2... the President to nominate a new Vice President" (R2); "Section 2. Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President, the President shall nominate a Vice President" (R5)

verifications.claim: A nomination under Section 2 of the 25th Amendment is subject to confirmation by a majority vote of both houses of Congress.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "confirmed by a majority Congressional vote" (R1); "confirmation by a majority vote in each chamber of Congress" (R2); "upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress" (R5)

verifications.claim: Under Section 3 of the 25th Amendment, the President may declare in writing they are unable to perform duties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "if the president tells... in writing that he is unable to perform his presidential powers and duties" (R1); "sending a written declaration... stating that he is unable to discharge them" (R2); "transmits... his written declaration that he is unable to discharge the powers and duties" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to Section 3 text and descriptions.

verifications.claim: A declaration under Section 3 makes the Vice President the Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the duties shall fall to the vice president as acting president until the president notifies them in writing otherwise" (R1); "until the President communicates that he is again able... the Vice President serves as Acting President" (R2); "and until he transmits... a written declaration to the contrary... discharged by the Vice President as Acting President" (R5)

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment authorizes the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet (or another body authorized by Congress) to declare the President unable to perform their duties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the vice president and a majority of... the 'principal officers of the executive departments'—... Cabinet secretaries—or... another body that Congress designates by law" (R2); matching text in R1, R5

verifications.claim: A declaration under Section 4 makes the Vice President the Acting President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the vice president immediately becomes acting president" (R1); "the Vice President immediately assumes such powers and duties as Acting President" (R2); "the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties... as Acting President" (R5)

verifications.claim: If the President disputes the incapacity under Section 4, Congress must decide the issue within 48 hours.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Congress must assemble within 48 hours... Unless Congress determines within 21 days" (R2); "assembling within forty-eight hours... within twenty-one days" (R5); same timeline (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify Congress assembles within 48 hours if not in session but decides within 21 days, contradicting 'decide within 48 hours'.

verifications.claim: A two-thirds vote in both houses is required to keep the Vice President in power under Section 4.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "by two-thirds vote of both Houses that the President is unable... the Vice President shall continue" (R2); "by a two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate" (R3); "by two-thirds vote of both Houses" (R5)

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been formally invoked.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been used" (R1); "Section 4, which has never been invoked" (R2); "Section 4 has never been used" (R6); "Section 4 has not been activated since... 1967" (R9)

verifications.claim: Section 2 of the 25th Amendment was used to appoint Gerald Ford in 1973 after Spiro Agnew resigned.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "invoked twice... Vice President Spiro T. Agnew's... resignations... Gerald Ford succeeded" (R2); "Gerald Ford replacing Vice President Spiro Agnew after his resignation in 1973" (R7)

verifications.claim: Section 2 of the 25th Amendment was used to appoint Nelson Rockefeller in 1974 after Ford became President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Section 2... invoked twice during the 1970s... Vice President Spiro T. Agnew's and President Nixon's resignations... Vice President Gerald Ford succeeded Nixon, resulting in a vice presidential vacancy" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Implied second use after Ford's ascension; historical context confirms Rockefeller in 1974.

verifications.claim: Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President Reagan in 1985 before surgery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Section 3... informally implemented once by President Ronald Reagan, in 1985... underwent surgery... transmitted a letter" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Detailed account confirms use for surgery.

verifications.claim: Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President George W. Bush in 2002 for medical procedures.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "On June 29, 2002, President George W." (snippet); "President George W. Bush—2002... On June 29, 2002... undergoing a routine colonoscopy" (R9)

verifications.claim: Section 3 of the 25th Amendment was used by President George W. Bush in 2007 for medical procedures.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "when he had another colonoscopy in 2007" (snippet); "President George W. Bush—2002 and 2007... On July 21, 2007... routine colonoscopy" (R9)
